title: Coach Twelve, Seat Sixty-One
subject: two strangers stuck for four hours on a Eurostar halted in a field outside Lille split the one tin of sardines, a squashed baguette and a clementine she had packed, swap numbers on the back of a ticket, and a year later book the same train, coach and seats on purpose, bringing two tins this time
caption: Bedroom-born indie pop, 2020s alternative pop with a home-studio feel. Chorus-soaked clean electric guitar arpeggios, a round fingered bass, a dry live drum kit with brushed snare, a soft Juno synth pad and small glockenspiel accents on the chorus. Warm home-recorded feel, light tape saturation, roomy drums, intimate double-tracked vocal in the chorus. Male tenor, soft and close, lifting into head voice, conversational in the verses. 104 BPM, D major. Shy, warm and quietly giddy. No trap beat, no autotune, no EDM drop, no stadium rock guitars, no orchestral strings.
lyrics:
[Intro - chorus guitar arpeggio and glockenspiel]

[Verse 1]
Stopped in a field somewhere outside of Lille
The trolley sold out and the lights went still
You pulled out a tin with a key on the lid
And said I've only got one, so you get half of it

[Pre-Chorus]
Half a baguette that you'd sat on by mistake
One clementine, and you pushed the bigger half my way

[Chorus]
Coach twelve, seat sixty-one
Four hours late and I didn't want it done
Oil on my fingers, salt on your sleeve
Stuck on a train that I didn't want to leave

[Verse 2]
The driver said sorry in French, then again
You translated badly and I laughed like a friend
You wrote down your number on the back of my ticket
In smudgy blue biro, I folded it into my pocket

[Pre-Chorus]
And when we rolled into London at ten
You said if it's ever this slow, call me then

[Chorus]
Coach twelve, seat sixty-one
Four hours late and I didn't want it done
Oil on my fingers, salt on your sleeve
Stuck on a train that I didn't want to leave

[Bridge - pad and brushed snare]
A year to the day, we both booked the same two seats
You held up two tins and said nobody's stuck, it's a treat

[Chorus]
Coach twelve, seat sixty-one
Right on time and I still don't want it done
Oil on my fingers, salt on your sleeve
Sharing a train that I don't want to leave

[Outro - glockenspiel and guitar, fading]
